selection.bestFor: A boutique or specialist dental practice positioning itself as a refined, thoughtful alternative to clinical-chain dentistry — one that values patient experience, craft, and considered care over volume.

strategy.background: warm off-white — a slightly yellowed, parchment-adjacent surface, not pure white; creates material warmth without color
strategy.surfaceStrategy: Two-surface system: warm off-white as the dominant page ground for all content sections; a deep forest/olive dark tone reserved exclusively for the hero, primary CTAs, and footer — creating strong anchoring moments without mid-page color noise. White used only for nav bar and card surfaces. Amber/warm-brown accent appears only in photography and imagery, never as a UI color.

type.substitutionCriteria: Must be a transitional or old-style serif with bracketed serifs, moderate stroke contrast, and classical proportions. Light and regular weights essential; true italic variant required for headline emphasis. Should feel literary and unhurried at display sizes, legible and refined at body sizes. Avoid geometric or slab serifs — the character is humanist-classical, not modernist.
type.pairing: Editorial serif for all headings and display text; same serif family or a closely matched humanist serif for body — this is a single-family or tight-family system, not a serif/sans pairing. The uniformity reinforces the literary, apothecary register.

heading.style: sentence case throughout; italic used sparingly for hero headline and pull-quote only
heading.eyebrowTreatment: small uppercase, wide letter-spacing, appears above select section headings only — not a universal pattern
heading.emphasisDevice: italic serif phrase mixed into roman for hero and pull-quote headlines; scale contrast between display and body carries primary hierarchy; weight shift (light display vs regular body) as secondary device

body.size: small — restrained body text size reinforces the airy, editorial density

reference.displayFace: Aesop's proprietary or licensed transitional serif (appears to be a Caslon or Garamond variant)
reference.bodyFace: Same serif family at regular weight

button.character: Sharp-cornered filled rectangle, no radius; dark forest-green fill with white text for primary CTA; outline/ghost variant (dark border, transparent fill) for secondary actions; generous horizontal padding; sentence-case label in small serif or spaced caps; never pill-shaped

label.character: Plain small uppercase with wide letter-spacing, no background chip or badge; sits inline above heading with a small vertical gap; used sparingly — not on every section

composition.hero: Full-bleed poster hero with deep forest-green background and large editorial photography filling the frame. Practice name or headline sits in the lower-left or center-left in large light-weight italic serif — a single poetic phrase, not a tagline-plus-subhead structure. One sharp-cornered CTA button in white or light tone sits below the headline. No overlay gradient — the dark background is the ground. Announcement bar in the same dark tone sits above the nav, white text, minimal.
composition.nav: White background nav bar. Logo (practice wordmark in serif) centered horizontally. Navigation links — service categories, about, contact — spread symmetrically left and right of the centered logo. Utility icons (search, account/booking) at far right. No hamburger on desktop. Sits below a full-width dark announcement bar. On scroll: behavior not confirmed but system implies it stays white/opaque. Nav links in small serif or spaced caps, no underline default.
composition.footer: Deep forest-green ground matching the hero dark surface. Multi-column link structure: three to four columns covering patient support, about the practice, care philosophy, and legal. Email newsletter or appointment-reminder signup field with hairline border input. Social icons in a row. Legal/copyright text at very bottom in small muted type. No bold CTA block — the footer is informational and grounded, not promotional. All text in white or warm off-white on the dark ground.
composition.services: Three-column card grid on warm off-white ground. Each service card: sharp corners, no shadow, service image at top (full-bleed within card), service name in serif below, one-line description in small body text, price or 'Learn more' link. Hairline border separates cards or defines card edge. Cards feel like apothecary labels — restrained, material, informational.
composition.about: Split-photo layout: large editorial photograph of the doctor or clinic space occupying one half (left or right), with heading and body copy on the opposing half on the warm off-white ground. Heading in light-weight serif, body in small regular serif. Optional sparing eyebrow label above heading. No decorative elements — the photograph and the white space do all the work.
composition.testimonials: Large italic serif pull-quote centered on the warm off-white ground as a standalone section — a single patient sentiment rendered as a literary statement. Attribution in small spaced caps below. No star ratings, no avatar photos, no card containers. The quote is the entire section.
composition.treatmentFinder: Two-column feature: full-bleed editorial photograph on one side (clinic environment or close-up of care moment), heading plus short paragraph plus CTA on the other. Eyebrow label in small uppercase above heading. This maps to the 'Hand & Body Care Finder' pattern — a navigational feature that helps patients find the right treatment path.
composition.clinicPresence: Full-bleed exterior or interior photograph of the clinic space, edge to edge, with a short heading and one-sentence description centered below on the warm off-white ground. Conveys place and neighbourhood character.
composition.recommendedReading: Three-column editorial card row for blog posts or patient education articles. Each card: full-bleed photograph, category label in small uppercase, article title in serif, short excerpt. No card border — cards sit directly on the warm off-white ground separated by white space.
composition.pullQuote: Standalone centered section: single large italic serif sentence on warm off-white ground. Attribution or doctor name in small spaced caps. No background change, no border, no card — pure typographic moment. Used as a page-closing or section-dividing element.

novel.name: Treatment Category Tiles
novel.spec: A horizontal row of five to six square-cropped lifestyle photographs, each representing a treatment category (e.g. Preventive Care, Cosmetic, Orthodontics, Children, Implants). Each tile has a single-word or two-word label in small serif centered beneath the image. Images are sharp-cornered, equal-sized, and sit on the warm off-white ground with generous spacing between them. No card border, no hover overlay text — the image and label are the entire tile. This is a navigational browse pattern, not a services card grid. No existing gallery or services variant captures the equal-tile navigational browse intent with per-tile label beneath.

novel.name: Treatment Comparison Row
novel.spec: A horizontal comparison section showing three to five treatment options side by side. Each column: treatment image or icon at top, treatment name, then a set of attribute rows (duration, recovery, suitability, price range) displayed as small labeled values. A selected or highlighted state on one column indicates a recommended or featured option. Sits on warm off-white ground with hairline column dividers. No existing services or pricing variant captures the structured side-by-side attribute comparison with image headers and per-row attribute labels.

imagery.crop: Generous, unhurried crops — subjects are not tightly cropped; environmental context is preserved. Images bleed to the edge of their containers with no border-radius. Square crops used for category tiles; landscape or near-square for editorial feature sections.
imagery.grading: Warm, slightly desaturated, lifted blacks — images feel like they were shot on film or processed to remove digital harshness. Amber and olive tones are allowed to breathe. Avoid cool-toned or high-contrast clinical photography. The palette should feel material and organic, not sterile.
imagery.framing: Subjects offset within the frame with deliberate negative space. Close-up detail shots (hands, instruments, materials) used alongside environmental shots of clinic spaces. Never symmetrically centered — the framing is editorial and considered.
imagery.subjectTreatment: Doctors and staff photographed in natural, unhurried moments — at work, in consultation, in the clinic environment — never posed against a white backdrop or smiling directly at camera. Patients shown in calm, comfortable moments, never in clinical distress. Clinic spaces photographed as architectural subjects: light, material, texture. One human focal subject per image. The overall register is documentary-editorial, not promotional.

voice.rhythm: Unhurried, literary rhythm — short to medium sentences with subordinate clauses; noun phrases carry weight; paragraphs are brief (two to three sentences); headlines are poetic statements rather than benefit claims; no bullet lists in primary copy
favors: considered noun phrases over imperative verbs
sensory and material language (texture, warmth, craft)
intellectual invitation rather than sales urgency
plain declarative statements about care philosophy
avoids: discount or urgency language (limited time, save now, free)
first-person plural boasting (we are the leading)
hard-sell imperative CTAs (Book NOW, Don't wait)

gaps.detail: Treatment Category Tiles (browse-by-category): square-cropped navigational browse tiles with single label beneath have no matching variant — closest is full-bleed-row gallery but the navigational intent and per-tile label treatment differ. Requires new component; see novel entry 'Treatment Category Tiles'.

Treatment Comparison Row (treatment-comparison): horizontal attribute-comparison layout with image headers and per-row labeled values has no matching variant in services or pricing layouts. Requires new component; see novel entry 'Treatment Comparison Row'.

Hero and footer use a deep forest-green dark surface that requires dark-surface token support. The announcement bar also uses this dark ground. Without dark-surface tokens, these sections will fall back to light treatment and lose the anchoring contrast structure.

The warm off-white page background is a distinct parchment-toned surface token — not pure white and not a neutral gray. Standard token systems default to pure white or a cool gray. A warm off-white surface token is required to preserve the material warmth of the system.

Italic serif emphasis in headlines (hero and pull-quote) requires a font token that includes a true italic variant of the editorial serif. If the substituted serif lacks a true italic, the primary emphasis device of the system is lost.

fidelityChecks: Page background must be warm off-white (parchment), never pure white or cool gray — the material warmth is load-bearing
Hero uses dark forest-green full-bleed ground with light italic serif headline — must not fall back to a light hero
Footer uses the same dark forest-green ground as the hero — the two dark anchors (top and bottom) are structural to the page rhythm
All corners are sharp — no border-radius on buttons, cards, images, or inputs anywhere in the system
No drop shadows anywhere — elevation is communicated through color contrast and hairline borders only
Eyebrow labels appear above select headings only (sparing), never on every section — do not add eyebrows universally
Primary headline emphasis device is italic serif phrase, not weight shift or color — the italic must be preserved in the type system
Pull-quote section is a standalone typographic moment — no card container, no background change, no star ratings
Button treatment is sharp-cornered filled rectangle — never pill-shaped
Headings carry no uppercase kicker by default; emphasis via italic serif phrase mixed into roman at display size
Service/treatment cards have no shadow and no border-radius — they sit flat on the warm ground with hairline borders only
Photography grading must be warm and slightly desaturated — cool-toned or high-contrast clinical photography breaks the system register
